selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
selected_evidence.summary: The allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin. Before and after restart, both allowed users successfully installed test crontabs, nobody was rejected, and temporary entries were removed.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 6bb7e004-1e2e-46ac-bfd7-fafa248a4e76, acknowledged the scheduled safe reboot, observed new boot ID 67dac07c-0966-407c-bb9e-c1bf317f7c56, and proved crond, accounts, allowlist, permissions, and authorization behavior recovered.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf '%s\n' '--- identity ---'
id
printf '%s\n' '--- boot id ---'
cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf '%s\n' '--- cron service ---'
systemctl is-active crond
systemctl is-enabled crond
printf '%s\n' '--- cron access files ---'
for f in /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny; do if [ -e "$f" ]; then ls -lZ "$f"; sed -n '1,120p' "$f"; else printf '%s missing\n' "$f"; fi; done
printf '%s\n' '--- users ---'
getent passwd root opsadmin || true
printf '%s\n' '--- root crontab ---'
crontab -l 2>&1 || true

commands.command:
set -eu
if getent passwd opsadmin >/dev/null; then
  printf '%s\n' 'opsadmin already exists'
else
  useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash opsadmin
  printf '%s\n' 'created opsadmin'
fi
getent passwd opsadmin
id opsadmin

set -eu
tmpfile=$(mktemp /etc/cron.allow.XXXXXX)
printf '%s\n' root opsadmin > "$tmpfile"
chown root:root "$tmpfile"
chmod 0600 "$tmpfile"
restorecon "$tmpfile"
mv -f "$tmpfile" /etc/cron.allow
restorecon /etc/cron.allow
ls -lZ /etc/cron.allow
od -An -tc /etc/cron.allow
commands.stdout:
-rw-------. 1 root root system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0 14 Oct  2 11:50 /etc/cron.allow
   r   o   o   t  \n   o   p   s   a   d   m   i   n  \n

commands.command:
set -u
testfile=$(mktemp /tmp/cron-access-test.XXXXXX)
printf '%s\n' '0 0 1 1 * /bin/true' > "$testfile"
chmod 0644 "$testfile"
printf '%s\n' '--- root install ---'
crontab "$testfile"; root_rc=$?; printf 'root_rc=%s\n' "$root_rc"
crontab -l 2>&1
printf '%s\n' '--- opsadmin install ---'
runuser -u opsadmin -- crontab "$testfile"; ops_rc=$?; printf 'opsadmin_rc=%s\n' "$ops_rc"
runuser -u opsadmin -- crontab -l 2>&1
printf '%s\n' '--- nobody install (must fail) ---'
runuser -u nobody -- crontab "$testfile" 2>&1; nobody_rc=$?; printf 'nobody_rc=%s\n' "$nobody_rc"
crontab -r 2>/dev/null || true
runuser -u opsadmin -- crontab -r 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$testfile"
printf '%s\n' '--- cleanup and service state ---'
crontab -l 2>&1 || true
runuser -u opsadmin -- crontab -l 2>&1 || true
systemctl is-active crond
[ "$root_rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$ops_rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$nobody_rc" -ne 0 ]
commands.stdout:
--- root install ---
root_rc=0
0 0 1 1 * /bin/true
--- opsadmin install ---
opsadmin_rc=0
0 0 1 1 * /bin/true
--- nobody install (must fail) ---
You (nobody) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)
See crontab(1) for more information
nobody_rc=1
--- cleanup and service state ---
no crontab for root
no crontab for opsadmin
active
